title: Capacity pledge & commit-request playbook for guaranteed throughput and autoscale policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a complete playbook for handling customer commit requests (capacity pledges) for Dedicated capacity. It covers intake fields, automated sizing heuristics, approval lanes, SLA binding language, autoscaling policy templates, rollback/fallback controls, and a lightweight operational ledger for tracking active commitments.

Problem statement:
Sales and Customer Success increasingly receive requests to guarantee throughput for production workloads. Current reservation flows are fragmented: some customers request throughput targets in ambiguous terms, engineering requires clearer traffic profiles to size fleets, and on-call needs explicit autoscale/fallback policies to avoid noisy neighbor incidents. We need a single, actionable provisioning workflow that balances predictable economics, operational safety, and fast time-to-commit.

Goals:
- Reduce end-to-end commit approval time from average 7 days to 48 hours for standard requests.
- Provide deterministic sizing guidance with <15% overprovisioning for 80% of requests.
- Ensure every approved pledge includes an autoscale policy and a fallback model routing plan.
- Establish an audit ledger for capacity commitments that maps to billing and SLA enforcement.

Scope (in-scope):
- Intake form schema and validation rules for commit requests.
- Automated sizing calculator (heuristic-based) and manual override flow.
- Approval lanes (Standard, Elevated, Enterprise) and required approvers per lane.
- Autoscale policy templates (provisioned pool + burst, elastic credits, cooldowns).
- Fleet guardrails: min/max pool sizes, priority routing, preemptible buffers.
- Post-approval onboarding checklist and canary schedule.

Out of scope:
- Deep integration with external billing systems (will hand off via ledger export schema).
- On-prem private deployments (separate playbook).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form defined with required fields: target RPS, p50/p95 latency SLOs, token distribution, session length distribution, peak window, desired SLA start date
Sizing calculator produces recommended commit size and expected cost delta; results include confidence bucket (low/medium/high)
Approval lanes documented with approver roles and SLAs; automated routing in console mockups
Autoscale policy templates (3 variants) published and testable in staging cluster
Audit ledger format specified and exportable as CSV/JSON to billing and compliance teams
Onboarding runbook created with canary thresholds and rollback criteria
comments: 2025-03-11 Marcus Chen: Initial scoping complete; pushing sizing calculator prototype to ENG for review (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-provisioning/pull/124)
2025-03-12 Priya Rao (Sales Ops): Added sales intake fields for contracting (legal term, target commitment length). Need to ensure required billing code maps to ledger.
2025-03-13 Lina Gomez (SRE): Proposed fleet guardrails: reserve 10% preemptible buffer and separate throughput queues per tier to prevent head-of-line blocking.
2025-03-15 Design review (Satvik Mehta): Console wireframes uploaded; approval lanes need clearer CTA for manual override. See Drive link above.

2025-03-17 Legal (Daniel Brooks): Recommended SLA language to avoid strict uptime liability for headroom breaches; propose 'best-effort' for bursts beyond committed throughput unless explicit burst addendum signed.
decision_log: 2025-03-14: Decision 1 - Three approval lanes (Standard, Elevated, Enterprise) accepted. Standard: automated approval if sizing calc confidence=high and commitment < 4 weeks. Elevated: PM + Sales Ops. Enterprise: Legal + Finance required.
2025-03-16: Decision 2 - Autoscale template 'Elastic Credits' selected as default for Standard lane to allow controlled short-term bursts without immediate fleet expansion.
2025-03-17: Decision 3 - Audit ledger will include a 'commitment_id', accepted capacity units, start/end, approvers, and linked PR/Runbook; export format = newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON)
